what: Per-module selftest wall time and exit code for the gatefly lane, measured in one sequential pass on this host. Written because a sibling lane was about to justify a design decision with a timeout figure attributed to this lane that this lane had never measured.
host_note: one sequential pass, CPU and GPU as configured on this machine, no warm cache between modules. Each module pays its own torch import.
finding: Every one of the 22 modules exits 0 and every plant passes, so ANY red under a cap is a false red. A 60 s cap turns 2 modules red and misreports 24 plants; a 300 s cap turns none red. So the FAILED / COULD-NOT-BE-RUN distinction is not hypothetical at the caps actually in use - it is the difference between 0 and 24 plants reading as broken.
concentration: The two slowest modules (mnk.py 285.2 s, ladder_probe.py 266.4 s) are 73.7% of the total cost while holding 8.4% of the plants. So a cheap full sweep is available by deferring two modules, and the cost column is worth having per module rather than in aggregate.
correction: This lane previously told the user and a sibling lane that metrics.py was the module grinding past ten minutes. That was WRONG: metrics.py runs in 1.0 s and is among the fastest here. The slow module is ladder_probe.py at 266.4 s, which sits between ladder.py and metrics.py alphabetically - the last line printed was ladder.py and metrics.py was assumed to be next. A guess about which module was running, reported as an observation.
not_verified: One run per module, so these are single samples with no variance estimate, and they include per-process torch import cost that a single-process runner would pay once. They do not measure how often a plant FIRES, which is the other column the light-loop cost item needs and which cannot be read from a passing run.
